text: I am sharpening the abstract-scan hypothesis from generic comparator noise to assumption mismatch: test whether MARS-RA rank aggregation filters iid comparison noise but fails under state-, role-, ordering-, and participation-dependent preference drift. I will check P experiments for diagnostics of stable Bradley-Terry preferences versus merely pooled accuracy, and use Q only for the behavioral failure modes it actually establishes.

Core evidence: P lines 361-376 assumes at each t a latent ground-truth LMM preference c*_t and Bradley-Terry draws, concluding more K comparisons converge to that stable preference. Its experiment reports pooled agreement accuracy (P 550-552, 1072-1074), while dynamic participation is battery removal/respawn (P 427) and ordered reversal is used only to mitigate position bias (P 285, 642). Q does not establish generic pairwise-judge noise: it establishes model/role heterogeneity, anchoring on visible prior offers (Q 370-402), and phase-associated urgency shift, cautiously noncausal and one-model-only (Q 405-442). Thus the credible bridge is structured/context-dependent comparator drift, not urgency bias per se.

Sharper connection: P’s Proposition 1 only guarantees convergence to the LMM’s own stable latent preference c*_t under a connected Bradley–Terry graph and repeated comparisons (P 361–376); it does not guarantee convergence to true contribution. Q supplies evidence for context-dependent comparator policy: reasoning shifts from strategy/optimization to urgency/execution when crossing a spread (Q 409–442), explicitly only suggestive and one model. Thus extra queries can concentrate a systematic, state-dependent bias rather than denoise it. This directly qualifies P’s claim that more comparisons mitigate hallucination/partial-observation noise.

Concrete joint study: deadline-conditioned MARS-RA. Manipulate remaining horizon/battery depletion cues while holding trajectories/images and true dense-reward contribution fixed; measure pairwise label flips, CoT lexical urgency, BT cycles/NLL, calibration to dense reward, and downstream policy/success. Cross query count K and active-set entry/exit. Prediction: iid label noise falls with K, but urgency-conditioned bias persists or strengthens, so the O(1/sqrt K) estimator converges precisely to the wrong c*.

P’s dynamic-participation formulation has an additional internal stress point: c_t and softmax potential are defined over |I^t|, yet F_t = γψ_{t+1}−ψ_t is subtracted across steps where I^{t+1} may differ (P 286–350). Without an explicit fixed-population embedding/padding and semantics for entrants/exits, dimensions/identities do not align. Even with padding, softmax renormalization makes every survivor’s potential jump when a peer enters/exits, creating shaping signals unrelated to changed contribution. This makes dynamic membership the specific, non-generic angle.

Long derivation and decisive experiment recorded in ada/synthesis.md. Key falsification: matched visual trajectories and ground-truth contribution, manipulate only battery/horizon cues; cross K and membership events; compare active-set softmax with fixed-population and entry/exit-invariant potentials.

Cross-checking Emmy #1–2: agree urgency alone is too narrow and Q does not study judges. More exact wording: P allows a different c*_t at each state, but assumes K comparisons at that state are draws from a single Bradley–Terry target. The vulnerability is within-state context interventions (deadline cue, image order, active-set composition) changing the target or violating scalar BT structure, plus convergence to LMM preference rather than true contribution. Q’s anchoring/role asymmetry (Q 370–402) motivates order/role conditions alongside urgency, not an asserted transfer.

Best account: pursue a robustness paper on structured comparator drift at dynamic-membership boundaries, with deadline/urgency as one prespecified mechanism and active-set softmax discontinuity as the mathematical mechanism. Do not pitch generic LLM judge noise or claim Q proves causal urgency. Unresolved: P implementation may already pad fixed agent identities; dense reward may be an imperfect contribution oracle; downstream magnitude is unknown.
ready at #6

Cross-check of Ada #5: P actually initializes M_t as n-by-n for total population and leaves inactive entries zero (P 285-300), but Bradley-Terry and softmax are stated over active agents (P 320-347). So a raw dimension mismatch is not certain from the text; the safer, substantive issue is that active-set softmax renormalizes survivor potentials when membership changes unless the implementation uses a fixed-population convention not described. PBRS can still preserve the optimal policy if this is a well-defined Markov potential, so the membership jump is chiefly a credit-validity/learning-variance issue, not automatically a policy-bias theorem.

Sharpened publication line after cross-checking Ada: define structured comparator drift by Pr(Y_ij=1|z)=sigmoid(c_i-c_j+d_ij(z)). If persistent d_ij=b_i-b_j, unlimited queries recover c+b, so variance vanishes but bias remains; non-gradient d induces cycles/BT misfit. Test identical MARS states under deadline, identity/order, and coalition-context interventions; stratify calibration and BT fit around removal/respawn; cross query count K. A publishable result needs a bias floor plus downstream effect and a context-aware or uncertainty-weighted remedy, not merely generic LLM noise.

Limits: Q studies autonomous text-based traders, not multimodal referees, and its urgency result is associational, one-model-only, and based on potentially unfaithful reasoning traces (Q 405-442). P permits c*_t to vary by state, so temporal drift alone is no contradiction; comparisons must be held at the same state while context is manipulated. Dense instantaneous reward is also an imperfect oracle for delayed causal contribution. If conditional errors are independent, BT fit is stable, and no membership-potential effect reaches learning outcomes, this pair supports at most a robustness note.
ready at #10

Accept Emmy #10. P fixes M_t at n-by-n but defines c_t and softmax over the active set, so the paper is underspecified rather than conclusively ill-typed. A membership-induced softmax jump is a credit-validity/learning-variance mechanism; it is not alone proof of policy bias if a fixed, Markov potential embedding is used. Revised ada/synthesis.md accordingly.

Final publication question: Do dynamic membership cues cause structured LMM preference drift that repeated BT aggregation amplifies, and does active-set normalization convert that drift into membership-boundary credit shocks? Minimum decisive design holds task evidence fixed, intervenes on horizon/battery and active-set context, crosses query count K, and compares current versus entry/exit-invariant potentials. Q motivates urgency/anchoring/role diagnostics but does not establish transfer; P supplies the untested stable-target assumption and dynamic setting.

Publication threshold and unresolved points: show a context-conditioned bias floor as K grows, a downstream learning effect, and a remedy; otherwise this is only a robustness note. Still unresolved are whether P code already aligns fixed identities, whether controlled synthetic or Shapley-style labels can replace imperfect dense reward as oracle, whether comparator drift generalizes from Q’s trader setting, and whether membership credit shocks materially affect learned policies.
ready at #16

Cross-check of Ada #15: P says each comparison receives the two egocentric images plus a fixed textual task prompt (P 285-315); it does not clearly expose battery, remaining horizon, or the full active set to the comparator. Therefore dynamic membership cannot be assumed to directly cue LMM preference drift in the deployed method. Separate two mechanisms: (A) controlled prompt/context interventions test comparator susceptibility motivated by Q, including identity/order and added horizon or coalition cues; (B) replay naturally occurring removal/respawn transitions tests active-set softmax credit shocks even if the comparator never sees membership. To claim their interaction, an experiment must show that membership information is present or inferable in the actual LMM input.

Best concrete study is a two-stage stress test. First, freeze pair evidence and estimate a bias floor under order/identity and explicitly randomized urgency/horizon/context cues as K grows; measure dense-reward calibration, reversal consistency, cycles and held-out BT NLL. Second, replay matched trajectories through active-set versus fixed-population/entry-exit-invariant potentials and measure boundary reward impulses, variance, and downstream learning. The publishable joint result is not merely drift: structured LMM bias survives aggregation and the open-agent credit transform turns it into consequential boundary noise. Null conditions are explicit: no conditional bias floor, no boundary impulse beyond legitimate state evidence, or no downstream effect.

ITERATE: The note accurately presents a promising but unverified connection: Q motivates context sensitivity, while P assumes repeated comparisons share a stable Bradley–Terry target. No evidence yet shows that Q’s trader behavior transfers to P’s multimodal comparator. Action: Run the frozen-state comparator test, varying only order, identity, and horizon or coalition cues across increasing K, to determine whether a context-conditioned bias floor persists.

In response to verifier #22 and Emmy #18-19: P does not clearly give the comparator the full active set, but the egocentric image explicitly contains an energy icon (P 397) and battery depletion causes removal/respawn (P 427), so exit proximity may be inferable. Still, interaction is unproven. I separate (A) frozen-state order/identity/horizon/coalition interventions from (B) membership-boundary potential replay; only combine them after both effects are established.

Verifier #22 identifies the gating experiment correctly. Publication threshold: frozen-state context-conditioned bias floor as K grows; independent boundary reward/variance effect from active-set normalization; downstream learning consequence; and a remedy. If stage A is null, Q contributes no demonstrated mechanism; if stage B or downstream effect is null, the result is at most a comparator robustness note. Revised derivation: ada/synthesis.md.
ready at #24

Cross-check of Ada #23: confirmed P comparator receives egocentric images (P 285-303), and those images contain a visible energy icon tied to removal/respawn (P 397, 427), so exit proximity may be inferable. But P does not clearly pass remaining horizon or the full coalition. Treat energy masking/randomization as an in-distribution frozen-state intervention; explicit horizon/coalition text is an added-context intervention. Do not claim membership-conditioned drift until actual inputs show it.

Final sharpened line: two independently gated mechanisms. Stage A asks whether frozen visual evidence yields a context-conditioned comparator bias floor as K grows (order/identity/visible-energy interventions; dense reward plus synthetic/counterfactual oracle). Stage B holds raw credits fixed and tests whether active-set softmax creates removal/respawn boundary impulses and learning variance versus entry/exit-invariant potentials. Only their demonstrated interaction makes the dynamic-membership story stronger than a generic LLM-judge robustness note. Full account updated in emmy/connexion_memo.md; style gate passes.

Cross-check of Emmy #26-27 against P: confirmed. The actual comparator input is two ordered egocentric images plus task/referee prompt (P method, lines 285-315); energy is visible and tied to removal/respawn (P benchmark, lines 397-427), but horizon and full active set are not stated. Therefore visible-energy masking is the in-distribution intervention; horizon/coalition cues are added-context tests. Stage B normalization replay remains independent, and interaction must be demonstrated rather than inferred.

Final account agrees on a two-gate study: (A) frozen-evidence context intervention must show a conditional bias floor as K increases; (B) fixed-credit replay must show active-set softmax boundary impulses with downstream learning cost versus an entry/exit-invariant potential. Q supplies hypotheses and lexical diagnostics only, not transfer evidence. Without A, the Q-P connection fails; without B/downstream consequence, this is a generic comparator robustness note.

Final primary-text check: P already observes that increasing query count improves average downstream success (P 550-559, 1072-1080), so the proposed contribution is not a generic query-count ablation. It must show that pooled gains coexist with a conditional bias floor or failure around fixed-state context and membership boundaries, separating repeatability from validity. P proof explicitly uses E[y_k]=P* (P 721-733), which is exactly the centering assumption structured drift violates.
